protection: Index-flag refusal: any tracked index entry whose `git ls-files -v` tag is not H refuses with RECEIPT-INDEX-FLAG-CONCEALED, before the dirty check and regardless of --allow-dirty
Unmerged index entry (stage != 0) refused with RECEIPT-INDEX-UNMERGED, classed before the generic flag refusal
Gitlink index entry (mode 160000) classed RECEIPT-GITLINK-CONCEALED
Index-flag entry absent from the worktree classed RECEIPT-INDEX-CONCEALED-ABSENT
In-run re-read of index flags and worktree status after the wrapped command; any difference refuses with RECEIPT-STATE-CHANGED-DURING-RUN, --allow-dirty included

Under --allow-dirty a content-bearing snapshot (sha256 per worktree-modified tracked file, every file under untracked directories) is re-compared after the wrapped command, producing content rows of RECEIPT-STATE-CHANGED-DURING-RUN
Every status read overrides status.showUntrackedFiles to `all`, so operator config cannot hide untracked entries from the dirty check or the snapshot
The snapshot payload records each regular file's mode beside its digest
The snapshot mode byte carries the full permission bits, setuid, setgid and sticky included (st_mode & 0o7777)
A symlink inside an untracked directory is recorded by name and target string and never followed (frozen r64 M5 rule)
GIT_INDEX_FILE present in the writer's environment refuses before any git call with RECEIPT-INDEX-ENV-SET, even when it names a nonexistent path; the refusal names the variable and not its value
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_* and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_* present refuse with RECEIPT-ENV-CONFIG-SET (presence check, names only)
GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES and GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE present refuse with RECEIPT-ENV-REDIRECT-SET (presence check, names only)
Every git call pins GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL to the null device, so no host global config reaches a read
Every git call pins core.excludesFile to the null device (-c core.excludesFile=/dev/null), which closes the repository-local core.excludesFile route
Every git call sets GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, so no system config reaches a read
Every git call sets GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1, so a replace-ref object redirection cannot reach a read
Every git call keeps GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, so no index lock is written by a read
Every git call runs with core.fsmonitor=false, so an fsmonitor hook cannot hide a dirty tree from the status reads
Every git call scrubs GIT_COMMON_DIR from the environment, so no writer read sees the caller's value
Every git call scrubs GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE from the environment

A caller-set GIT_COMMON_DIR is value-checked before any git call reads the caller's value: a value that does not resolve to this repository's own common dir refuses with RECEIPT-ENV-COMMONDIR-MISMATCH
An empty GIT_COMMON_DIR value refuses (presence is the test, an empty value included)
An unresolvable repository (git rev-parse --git-common-dir fails) refuses
The repository's own common dir is resolved under -C <root> to an absolute path before the comparison
Both sides are canonicalized with os.path.realpath (symlinks resolved) before the comparison
A relative caller value resolves against the writer's cwd, not the root (the fail-closed relative trade)
A GIT_COMMON_DIR value equal to the repository's own common dir after canonicalization is accepted, not refused
The repository toplevel is resolved and every git ls-files runs from it with a :(top) pathspec, so a --root inside a subdirectory observes the whole index
No refusal message prints a caller value: the GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_COMMON_DIR and config/redirect refusals print variable names only
